title: Application Load Balancer: traffic is a separate layer
outcome: Configure listeners, target health, and request routing without confusing liveness with readiness.
useCase: Public Rails traffic and rolling deployments.
benefits: Central traffic routing and health-based distribution.
drawbacks: Proxy headers, timeouts, and health contracts need configuration.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: A running process is not automatically a ready target.

trace.title: HTTPS listener
trace.detail: An ALB accepts HTTP(S) traffic and forwards it according to listeners/rules to target groups. The target group knows where application targets live and how health is checked. A listening app port alone does not prove the app should receive traffic.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Client connects → TLS listener → routing rule → healthy target → Rails → response. On a 502/503/504, identify whether there were no healthy targets, a connection/protocol issue, or a slow target/dependency.

During deployment, allow draining and graceful shutdown so an old target can finish appropriate in-flight work before termination.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A health path that requires user login can mark every target unhealthy. A constant OK may hide failed startup dependencies. Sticky sessions can conceal session/storage assumptions rather than repair them.
